description: Parse nginx combined access logs (data/access.log) into ECS. The 'before' side of the migration: note how much of the work is grok, and how much of the enrichment (user_agent, geoip) is pipeline-time and therefore fixed at index time.

grok.description: The URI is matched with DATA (non-greedy), anchored on ' HTTP/', NOT with NOTSPACE. 300 requests in this dataset have a space inside the URI (scanners sending `/product?id=1\x22 OR \x221\x22=\x221` across five HTTP methods), and NOTSPACE fails on every one of them.

date.description: The combined format has second resolution only. Anything needing sub-second ordering must use access.json.log and its $msec field instead.

script.description: Split path from query by hand. The uri_parts processor expects an absolute URI and does not reliably handle a bare request target containing unencoded spaces, which is exactly what the scanner traffic here sends.
script.source: String u = ctx._tmp.uri_raw; int q = u.indexOf('?'); if (q < 0) { ctx.url.path = u; } else { ctx.url.path = u.substring(0, q); ctx.url.query = u.substring(q + 1); }

set.description: ECS wants total response bytes; the combined format only gives us the body
remote_user is '-' throughout this dataset (no HTTP basic auth); only set user.name when there is a real value

remove.description: nginx writes '-' for an absent referrer; drop the field rather than indexing a sentinel value that would show up in aggregations

geoip is deliberately absent: the client IPs are synthetic, so a real GeoLite2 lookup returns whatever those ranges happen to map to. Add a geoip processor here if you want to compare against a ClickHouse dictionary, but do not read meaning into the answers.
